steps.say: Crohn disease is treated with medicines until its complications take over. A scarred narrowing, tunnels into nearby organs, trapped pus, a dangerously dilated colon or a child who stops growing all point toward the operating theatre.
steps.tx: Surgery is indicated for **fibrostenotic** (scar-narrowed) stricture, **fistulising disease** (tunnelling infection) with abscess, toxic megacolon and **growth failure** (stalled childhood growth), while active luminal inflammation without these complications stays medical under gastroenterology care with close follow-up and timely escalation if complications appear.

vis.alt: Illustration comparing patchy full-wall Crohn inflammation with continuous surface ulcerative colitis.
vis.caption: Crohn versus colitis: skip lesions, transmural inflammation and cobblestone mucosa favour Crohn disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A short scarred segment in otherwise quiet bowel need not be removed. Slitting it lengthwise and sewing it crosswise widens the channel and preserves every centimetre of absorptive gut.
steps.tx: Short strictures under **10 cm** (ten centimetres) in quiescent bowel suit **Heineke-Mikulicz** (crosswise widening) **stricturoplasty** (bowel-sparing repair), while longer ones take **Finney** (U-shaped) or side-to-side isoperistaltic stricturoplasty to preserve length and avoid short bowel syndrome entirely and keep the patient off lifelong parenteral nutrition.

steps.say: The commonest operation removes the diseased last loop of small bowel with the start of the colon. Joining healthy ends restores continuity, and a newer join placed away from the blood supply side lowers the chance of return.
steps.tx: **Ileocolic resection** (terminal ileum with caecum removal) takes the diseased segment with primary joining of ends, and **Kono-S** (mesentery-sparing join) antimesenteric functional end-to-end anastomosis lowers surgical recurrence at the join in long-term follow-up studies across specialist inflammatory bowel centres worldwide.

steps.say: Tracts around the anus are mapped under anaesthesia before any cutting. Loose threads keep the tunnels drained while biologic drugs heal the bowel from inside. Removing the rectum is a last resort for a destroyed organ.
steps.tx: Complex perianal disease needs **examination under anaesthesia** (mapped probing asleep) with **seton** (loose draining thread) drainage plus **anti-TNF** (biologic healing drug) therapy, reserving proctectomy for a destroyed incontinent rectum that cannot be salvaged by any lesser operation despite optimal medicines and drainage.

steps.say: Bubbles of air in the urine with infections that never clear point to a tunnel between bowel and bladder. Scans confirm the connection. The bowel segment comes out and the bladder wall is repaired, but the bladder itself stays.
steps.tx: **Enterovesical fistula** (bowel-to-bladder tunnel) shows **pneumaturia** (air bubbles in urine) with recurrent urinary infections, confirmed by contrast imaging, and needs bowel segment resection with bladder cuff repair rather than cystectomy, preserving bladder capacity and function for a normal life afterwards.

steps.say: A colon that balloons under toxic inflammation can perforate without warning. When the width passes six centimetres with fever and a racing pulse, the whole colon comes out at once and no join is attempted.
steps.tx: **Toxic megacolon** (poisoned dilated colon) with transverse colon over **6 cm** (six centimetres) plus systemic toxicity needs urgent **subtotal colectomy** (near-total colon removal) with ileostomy, avoiding primary anastomosis in the emergency setting because an emergency leak frequently proves fatal in these sick patients.

steps.say: The single biggest favour a patient can do the join is to stop smoking. Half a year after surgery the camera goes back to grade the new connection, and early changes trigger protective drugs before symptoms return.
steps.tx: Smoking doubles postoperative recurrence, so **smoking cessation** (quitting tobacco) is prescribed firmly, and **6-month** (six month) colonoscopy with **Rutgeerts score** (join recurrence grading) directs timely prophylaxis with thiopurines or anti-TNF before any symptoms have a chance to return after the operation.

steps.say: Pus trapped beside the bowel is drained through the skin first, not cut out in the heat of infection. Antibiotics calm the tissues while nutrition is rebuilt. The definitive operation follows weeks later on quiet ground.
steps.tx: **Intra-abdominal abscess** (trapped pus beside bowel) over **3 cm** (three centimetres) gets **percutaneous drainage** (skin-needle drain) with antibiotics first, and resection follows after **6 to 8 weeks** (six to eight weeks) once sepsis has fully resolved and nutrition is rebuilt.
